detail.longDescription: In this example, is it guaranteed that the setTimeout in function Second() will always execute immediately after all the synchronous code in its caller (here, First() ) completes? That is barring, any additions to the call stack after First is invoked and before it invokes Second . Is there any way that the setTimeout could execute before the synchronous code of First() completes. function First() { console.log("Invoked First which is now invoking second"); let a = []; let x = Second(); console.log("First after return from Second"); let start = Date.now(); /* Synchronous garbage code to take more time that 1ms. */ for(let i=0; i<100000;i++) { a.push(i % 276);} a = a.join('-'); console.log(`Elapsed synchronous delay is ${Date.now()-start}ms`); console.log(`x is ${x}`); } function Second() { console.log("Invoked Second which is now setting 1ms timeout to invoke CallBack."); setTimeout( CallBack,0); return "Return from second." } function CallBack() { console.log("Hello, from the CallBack."); } First();
